source: climate_indices library reference output (standard Palmer); Wells, Goddard & Hayes reference C++ (scPDSI)
subset_description: Palmer drought index outputs for 344 US climate divisions, monthly, January 1895 through December 2022 (1536 values per array). Two provenance groups. (1) Standard Palmer -- pdsi.npy, phdi.npy, pmdi.npy, zindex.npy, alphas.npy, betas.npy, gammas.npy, deltas.npy -- generated from the library's own Palmer implementation against NCEI nClimDiv input data. (2) Self-calibrating Palmer -- scpdsi.npy, scphdi.npy, scpmdi.npy, sczindex.npy, and scdurfact.npy (4 values: wetm, wetb, drym, dryb) -- generated from the Wells, Goddard & Hayes reference C++ implementation. Inputs for both are precips.npy and pet.npy (inches) with per-division AWC from palmer_awc.json, calibration period 1931-1990.
citation: Palmer, W. C., 1965: Meteorological Drought. U.S. Weather Bureau Research Paper No. 45, 58 pp. Self-calibrating variant: Wells, N., Goddard, S., and Hayes, M. J., 2004: A Self-Calibrating Palmer Drought Severity Index. Journal of Climate, 17(12), 2335-2351.
notes: Checksum computed from division 0101 only (cat $(ls *.npy | sort) | shasum -a 256); it changed at fixture_version 1.1.0 because the sc* arrays were added to that directory. Full fixture contains 344 divisions. Standard-Palmer provenance was added retroactively in v2.4.0. SCPDSI GENERATION (added 2026-08-08, issue #719): produced by the Sibada/scPDSI reference C++ (Wells, Goddard & Hayes), which is GPLv3 while this project is BSD-3-Clause -- the oracle was built and run entirely outside this repository and only these numeric arrays were committed; no GPL source, headers, shim code or build scripts are distributed here. The harness shimmed four Rcpp symbols (NumericVector, NumericMatrix, Rf_error, Rf_warning) via include shadowing so pdsi.cpp and pdsi_ext.cpp compiled byte-identical to upstream, and fed inch-unit input directly rather than through the reference's millimetre entry point. HARNESS VALIDATION: running the same binary in standard-PDSI mode reproduces the committed zindex.npy for all 344 divisions at atol=5e-5, confirming the water balance, CAFEC coefficients, K-factors, unit handling and calibration window are correct. SC-PATH OFF-BY-ONE: the reference is inconsistent about the period index handed to CalcOneX -- CalcOrigK (standard path) converts it to 0-based, while CalcZ (self-calibrating path) passes the 1-based month from vals_mat column 1 straight through. Since CalcOneX indexes with n = (year-1)*12 + period_number, every self-calibrating write to columns 8-12 lands one row high, and the final period writes one past the end of the matrix. Only the Z-index is read from those columns, so only sczindex.npy was affected; scpdsi/scphdi/scpmdi come from Rext_output_X, which uses its own sequential counter and is correct on both paths. The harness compensates by reading column 8 at row i+1 in self-calibrating mode and allocating a slack row so the final period's value is preserved rather than overflowing. Verified after correction: sczindex/zindex is constant within each of the wet and dry branches to 8.5e-07 across all 344 divisions, which is what the algorithm predicts since the per-month K factor cancels. IMPORTANT -- the sc* arrays are NOT comparable to pdsi.npy/phdi.npy/pmdi.npy: those come from an NCEI Fortran (pdi.f) lineage while the sc* arrays come from the Wells lineage, and the two use different spell-selection state machines that disagree on roughly 6.3% of months by up to 8 PDSI units. On those disputed months the NCEI-lineage values are closer to NOAA operational data 88% of the time (see tests/fixture/nclimdiv). Consequently scpdsi() must implement the Wells recursion to match these fixtures; see epic #716.
